title: Two Thousand Dollars and a Barn: Wilson Greatbatch's Pacemaker Years
conflicts: Medtronic licence year: 1960 (MIT Technology Review; implied by his oral history) vs 1961 (NAE memorial tribute); the story gives no year. Leaving work: he says he 'quit all my jobs' (IEEE oral history, 2000); MIT TR says Taber declined the liability and he set out on his own; NAE says only that Taber did not support the work; the story uses his account plus the Taber refusal. Battery life: he says rated six years but few ran more than two; story uses his figures. Resistor year: 1956 (MIT TR, UB, NAE) vs 'late 1950s' (Lemelson-MIT).
notes: Core account from Greatbatch's own IEEE History Center oral history (2000). The well-known 'elation' quotation comes from his book, which could not be read online, so it is not used. Company field names the barn workshop because Wilson Greatbatch Ltd was founded only in 1970; the pacemaker was licensed to Medtronic.
